value: at every alternating-temperature pair tested, seeds germinated only under the light/dark cycle and not in continuous darkness (the text reads this as more restricted than C. hololeuca and C. pachystachya, which germinated somewhat in darkness under alternating temperatures)
method: germination of seeds in Petri dishes under light/dark (12 h/12 h) and continuous dark at constant 25 C and several alternating temperature pairs
conditions: seeds from Mata de Santa Genebra, southeastern Brazil (no collection date given), cleaned and kept about two months at about 9 C, surface-sterilised in 5% hypochlorite; usually four replicates of 20 seeds per treatment on moist filter paper in Petri dishes; 12 h light (fluorescent, about 20 mmol m-2 s-1) at the higher temperature / 12 h dark at the lower temperature ('light/dark'); dark dishes in opaque black polyethylene bags; about six weeks, radicle 1 mm scored weekly; arcsine-transformed ANOVA with Tukey 5%; germination percentages are in Table 1, which is an image on the page and was not read as text; the paper's constant-25 C statement for the three Cecropia species is that no germination occurred in darkness; the next sentence says a similar pattern was seen under natural conditions in the forest; the paper prints the name C. glazioui

method: germination of seeds in Petri dishes under light/dark (12 h/12 h) and continuous dark at constant 25 C and alternating temperature pairs

method: germination of fresh seeds on 1% water agar in Petri dishes in light (12 h cool white fluorescent) and in the dark (dishes in two layers of aluminium foil, checked once at the end) at constant temperatures 5 to 25 C (fresh-seed dark tests at 5, 15 and 25 C only)
conditions: three replicates of 20 seeds per test because well-developed seed was limited; 22.2 umol m-2 s-1; tests ended after 5 weeks followed by viability checks; seeds collected in September 2014 and 2015 at PuYong Pass (about 4,550 m), Yunnan, from at least 10 plants; generalized linear models with Bonferroni post hoc tests, the Figure 1 caption gives temperature, dry after-ripening and light each significant (p < 0.001); the Methods do not assign the dark incubations to a year (the Results place them under 2015); the same paper finds fresh seeds had a light requirement for germination overall, cold stratification and dry after-ripening reduced it, and P. sikkimensis dark germination at 25 C is the exception to that requirement
